lesson_title: Selling on Trust: The Book of Names
hook_text: Every township shop had the exercise book under the counter. Accounting just gave it superpowers.
clip_script: Every township shop that ever gave credit had one: the exercise book under the counter. A page for each person. Mrs Dube's page. The Naidoos' page. Buy now, pay month end — and the shopkeeper writes it down, because memory is generous and business cannot afford generous. That page-per-person book is the Debtors Ledger. But Thabo needs a second view: at month end he wants ONE number for what the whole street owes. Pages for the people, one line for the street — and here is the beautiful lock: add up all the pages, and the total MUST equal the street's one line. If the two counts ever differ, a promise got lost or doubled somewhere.
visual_style: A worn exercise book morphing into a clean ledger: name-pages fanning out, then stacking into a single glowing control line, with a padlock clicking when the totals match.
pacing: Warm storytelling open, brisk two-view build, satisfying click on the lock.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — invoices, credit notes, and the month that balances.
